panels.title: CPU utilization
panels.description: Whole-host CPU busy percentage, sampled over a 1s window each probe (psutil cpu_percent). 100% = every logical core saturated. Sustained highs here are a compute bottleneck.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, value FROM host_metrics WHERE metric='cpu_percent' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time
targets.queryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, value FROM host_metrics WHERE metric='cpu_percent' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time

panels.title: Load average (1m / 5m / 15m)
panels.description: System run-queue load. The M2 has 8 cores, so a load above 8 means processes are waiting for CPU — a saturation signal that complements CPU%. 1m is reactive, 15m is the trend.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, metric AS metric, value FROM host_metrics WHERE metric IN ('load_1m','load_5m','load_15m') AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time
targets.queryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, metric AS metric, value FROM host_metrics WHERE metric IN ('load_1m','load_5m','load_15m') AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time

panels.title: Memory used %
panels.description: Percentage of physical RAM in use (active + wired + compressed). On macOS free RAM is always near zero by design, so this — not 'free' — is the memory pressure gauge. Read it alongside swap below.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, value FROM host_metrics WHERE metric='mem_used_percent' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time
targets.queryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, value FROM host_metrics WHERE metric='mem_used_percent' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time

panels.title: Swap + wired memory (MB)
panels.description: Swap used (the headline memory-pressure signal — non-zero means RAM demand exceeded physical memory) plotted with wired memory (kernel-locked, non-swappable). Rising swap on an always-on box is the bottleneck most worth chasing.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, metric AS metric, value FROM host_metrics WHERE metric IN ('swap_used_mb','mem_wired_mb') AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time
targets.queryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, metric AS metric, value FROM host_metrics WHERE metric IN ('swap_used_mb','mem_wired_mb') AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time

panels.title: Disk I/O (bytes/sec)
panels.description: Per-second disk read/write throughput, derived from cumulative byte counters diffed across probes. Spikes correlate with model loads, ChromaDB writes, and SQLite WAL flushes — a storage bottleneck shows here.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, metric AS metric, value FROM host_metrics WHERE metric IN ('disk_read_bps','disk_write_bps') AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time
targets.queryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, metric AS metric, value FROM host_metrics WHERE metric IN ('disk_read_bps','disk_write_bps') AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time

panels.title: Network I/O (bytes/sec)
panels.description: Per-second network in/out throughput, derived from cumulative counters diffed across probes. Useful for spotting relay/sync saturation or unexpected egress. Mostly loopback traffic on this box.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, metric AS metric, value FROM host_metrics WHERE metric IN ('net_in_bps','net_out_bps') AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time
targets.queryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, metric AS metric, value FROM host_metrics WHERE metric IN ('net_in_bps','net_out_bps') AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time

panels.title: Memory pressure level (the verdict)
panels.description: macOS kernel memory-pressure level: 1 normal (green), 2 warning (amber), 4 critical (red). This — not swap used — is whether memory is actually a bottleneck. Swap can sit non-zero for days at level 1 with no impact; sustained 2/4 is real pressure worth acting on.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, value FROM host_metrics WHERE metric='mem_pressure_level' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time
targets.queryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, value FROM host_metrics WHERE metric='mem_pressure_level' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time

panels.title: Swap activity (bytes/sec)
panels.description: TRUE anonymous-swap churn from vm_stat Swapins/Swapouts, diffed to a rate. This is the signal that distinguishes static swap (cold pages parked in the swap file, harmless) from active thrash (the machine paging anonymous memory in and out under pressure). Flat zero here while swap_used is non-zero = not a bottleneck.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, metric AS metric, value FROM host_metrics WHERE metric IN ('swap_in_bps','swap_out_bps') AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time
targets.queryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, metric AS metric, value FROM host_metrics WHERE metric IN ('swap_in_bps','swap_out_bps') AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time

panels.title: Compressed memory (MB)
panels.description: Size of the macOS memory compressor pool. The kernel compresses cold anonymous pages here before resorting to the swap file, so a rising compressor is the earlier-warning pressure signal — it grows before swap activity starts.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, value FROM host_metrics WHERE metric='mem_compressed_mb' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time
targets.queryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, value FROM host_metrics WHERE metric='mem_compressed_mb' AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time

panels.title: Top processes by RSS (latest probe)
panels.description: The processes holding the most resident memory at the most recent probe — the 'what is actually eating RAM' answer. On this box the top consumers are usually macOS indexing/media daemons and desktop apps, not the Jarvis services; this panel makes that attribution explicit instead of guessable.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT name, pid, ROUND(rss_mb,0) AS rss_mb FROM host_process_metrics WHERE ts=(SELECT MAX(ts) FROM host_process_metrics) ORDER BY rss_mb DESC
targets.queryText: SELECT name, pid, ROUND(rss_mb,0) AS rss_mb FROM host_process_metrics WHERE ts=(SELECT MAX(ts) FROM host_process_metrics) ORDER BY rss_mb DESC

panels.title: RSS by process over time
panels.description: Per-process resident memory over time for the top consumers captured each probe. Use this to catch a transient balloon — e.g. ollama loading a model, or a routine spiking a service — that a single snapshot would miss. Series are by process name; many short-lived names is normal.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, name AS metric, rss_mb AS value FROM host_process_metrics WHERE julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time
targets.queryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, name AS metric, rss_mb AS value FROM host_process_metrics WHERE julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time

panels.title: External dependency latency (ChromaDB / embed / Graphiti)
panels.description: Per-dependency round-trip latency sampled every 60s by health-probe via the vec-server /probe endpoint. chroma = persistent-client heartbeat; embed = one Ollama embedding call (NAS); graph = Neo4j connectivity check. A gap means the dependency was unreachable that cycle (see Errors & Health timeline).

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, REPLACE(metric,'_latency_ms','') AS dependency, value FROM host_metrics WHERE metric IN ('chroma_latency_ms','embed_latency_ms','graph_latency_ms') AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time
targets.queryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s',ts) AS INTEGER) AS time, REPLACE(metric,'_latency_ms','') AS dependency, value FROM host_metrics WHERE metric IN ('chroma_latency_ms','embed_latency_ms','graph_latency_ms') AND julianday(ts) >= julianday($__from/1000,'unixepoch') AND julianday(ts) < julianday($__to/1000,'unixepoch') ORDER BY time
